answer: Operators lock a bond scaling with the square of their agent count. One agent costs a small stake; ten agents under one operator cost a hundred times that stake for a full epoch. Identity binds credential to funding source, so fresh keys never reset the multiplier, only enlarge exposure. A nebula of cheap identities becomes a capital bill paid while earning nothing, and one slashable fault forfeits the cluster. A fake army reaches the nadir of return per unit of capital, while honest operators with few seats stay solvent. Faking one more actor costs what being one costs, the reef of Sybil.
